title: THE GOD WHO BROUGHT YOU OUT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Keep my commands and follow them. I am the LORD. Do not profane my
holy name, for I must be acknowledged as holy by the Israelites. I am
the LORD, who made you holy and who brought you out of Egypt to be
your God. I am the LORD'" - Lev 22:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes by telling us the order of things. Look carefully.
God does not say, "Keep my commands so that I will rescue you." He says
He is the LORD who made them holy and who brought them out of Egypt.

The rescue came first. The commands come after.

That is the shape of grace throughout Scripture, and it is easy to get
backwards. Israel was not delivered from Egypt because they obeyed;
they obeyed because they had been delivered. Every command in
Leviticus rests on that foundation.

Dear friend, if you have been quietly trying to earn God's favour, let
this settle you. Paul writes that God demonstrated His love in this:
while we were still sinners, Christ died for us (Rom 5:8). We love
because He first loved us (1 John 4:19). We are saved by grace through
faith, not by works - and then created in Christ Jesus to do good works
(Eph 2:8-10).

Obedience is not the price of God's love. It is the response to it.

Four times in this chapter God has said, "I am the LORD, who makes you
holy." He said it because we so quickly forget. Let it be the last
thing you carry away from Leviticus 22.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I obeying God to earn His love or because I already have it?
2. What is my personal "brought out of Egypt" - how has God rescued me?
3. How would remembering grace change my obedience this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You rescued me before You ever asked anything
of me. Let my obedience flow from gratitude, never from fear. Amen.
